Euphoric

/yoo-FOR-ik/ · adjective

Hear It

What It Means

Euphoric means in a sustained state of intense elation and well-being, often almost dreamlike.

Euphoric means in a sustained state of intense elation and well-being, often almost dreamlike. For a week after her first book was accepted, Dana walked around euphoric, grinning at strangers on the bus.

Worked Example

Back on Earth after six months on the space station, Commander Reyes kept catching herself smiling at nothing. Gravity felt like a gift, grocery stores seemed miraculous, and even a traffic jam delighted her. The flight surgeon told her that returning crews often spend their first weeks euphoric — riding a long, dreamy high that no single moment can explain.

Reyes's weeks-long, free-floating glow — attached to everything and nothing in particular — is the sustained elevated state that euphoric names.

How Strong Is It? — content → euphoric → rapturous

content vs. euphoric

content vs. euphoric: Content is quiet satisfaction; euphoric is a soaring, intense high of well-being that colors everything around it.

rapturous vs. euphoric

rapturous vs. euphoric: Rapturous pushes past even euphoric — joy so consuming that a person seems swept entirely away by it.

Build the Word

The pieces

Prefix — eu-

Prefix — eu-: good, well (Greek)

Root — phor

Root — phor: carrying, bearing (Greek pherein)

Suffix — -ic

Suffix — -ic: relating to; characterized by

Put it together

Put it together: Euphoric joins the Greek prefix eu-, 'good or well,' to the root pherein, 'to carry or bear' — the same root hiding in metaphor ('carried across') and periphery ('carried around'). To be euphoric is literally to be 'borne along well': carried through your days on a current of intense well-being.

Use the root in a new word: periphery

Use the root in a new word: periphery: The periphery is the edge 'carried around' a center — the same Greek root pherein, 'to carry,' that lets a euphoric person feel borne along on well-being.
